statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is moderate at 36, carrying an unchanged rates, energy and US-Iran position from Friday's settlement.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z Friday and reopens Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly nineteen hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the backdrop. This hour's re-verification strengthened the index evidence: the 29,308.86 close, +0.33%, was cross-checked against separately reported Friday moves in the S&P 500 to 7,674.37, +0.43%, the Nasdaq Composite to 26,180.45, +0.43%, and the Dow to 53,277.01, +0.98%, while a third-party quote provider again returned an unsupported Nasdaq-100 level near 29,995 and was discarded. VIX at 14.89, the 2Y/10Y/30Y curve at 4.24%/4.74%/5.28%, WTI at 87.06 and Brent at 94.39 were all re-confirmed unchanged, as was the week-ahead catalyst stack: Core PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday, Nvidia after the Wednesday close, and Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on Friday. Nothing in that stack falls inside this horizon, and none of it is observed price-path evidence, so it is carried as Stress and Confidence rather than as Tail.
headline: Sixth consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, with Friday's cash NDX close of 29,308.86, +0.33%, now corroborated by separately reported S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Dow moves.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run to 2026-08-23T03:00:00Z. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. That settlement is now supported by three independent Friday index readings: the S&P 500 at 7,674.37, +0.43%, the Nasdaq Composite at 26,180.45, +0.43%, and the Dow at 53,277.01, +0.98% on healthcare strength. One quote provider again returned a materially higher Nasdaq-100 level near 29,995 while displaying its own delayed-data warning; that figure is inconsistent with every corroborating source and was discarded. The carried backdrop is rates-led rather than equity-led. The 30-year Treasury yield closed at 5.28%, near its highest since 2007, the 10-year at 4.74% testing 20-month highs and the 2-year at 4.24%, after a week in which a doubled Treasury buyback programme delivered only brief relief. Beneath the index, the week split: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell roughly 5% while software and Dow-side names finished Friday higher, and delayed weekend context shows semiconductors soft against firmer megacap software. Conflicting internals of that kind lower directional conviction and are scored as Stress, not as the persistent one-way structure Tail is defined on. VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.00% and near the base of a 14.77-15.95 range. Crude was little changed at 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent as reporting described indirect US-Iran messaging and Oman-mediated talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with no fresh escalation priced. The coming week carries Core PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday at 12:30Z, Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 results after the Wednesday cash close, and Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole appearance since taking office in May, on Friday at 14:00Z. Every one of those is a scheduled checkpoint beyond this horizon. Under the standing definition, Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful retracement, and a market that cannot trade cannot produce one; Tail is therefore published flat at 4 with EA_ON mapped in all twenty-four slots, while Stress traces 36 down to a 34 weekend trough and back up to 42 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the Sunday reopen. No danger window is published, because no evidence-based window exists inside a closed market.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 20 hourly assessments are available and 4 clock-hours, all in the 21 August overnight and late-morning windows, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the early European morning, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, then a step down to 10, 5 and finally 4 as the venue moved into its 21:00Z Friday halt and stayed there. Stress traced the same arc in reverse scale, easing from the high fifties to the mid thirties as equity-structure risk was replaced by carried rates, energy and weekend headline risk. No danger window was published in any of those hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the horizon ends at 2026-08-23T03:00:00Z, roughly nineteen hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress eases from 36 to a 34 trough through the quietest weekend hours and then climbs back to 42 by the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens; its composition is unchanged, with the 30-year at 5.28% near a 2007 high, the 10-year at 4.74% testing 20-month highs, crude held near 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse. Confidence starts at 86, one point above the previous hour on the added independent corroboration of Friday's index moves, and decays to 79 by the final slot as the verified settlement data ages. Dominant mode is normal in every slot. The first genuine test of the coming week arrives well beyond this horizon, with Core PCE and the Q2 GDP revision on Wednesday, Nvidia after the Wednesday close, and Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on Friday.
